subject: Hosted vs Dedicated — latency/throughput decision follow-up
messages:

Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Discovery — FinPay latency & throughput needs (post-call recap)

Thanks again for taking the time today, Marcos — good conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps: 

Summary of what we heard:
- Target p95 latency: <= 200 ms end-to-end for single-turn requests
- Expected steady-state throughput: ~300 requests/sec (spikes up to ~450 rps)
- Average input length: ~120 tokens; batch size typically = 1
- Data: no sensitive PII; standard GDPR concerns, will need SOC2 + audit log access

Initial recommendation (high level):
- Two viable paths: Hosted API with reserved capacity (fastest to production) OR Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) if you need absolute isolation and predictable tail latencies. Private VPC/on-prem not required based on current compliance ask.

Proposed next steps:
1) Can you confirm whether 200 ms p95 is a hard SLA or a target?
2) Share a 24-hr sample of traffic shape (timestamps + size) — that will let us sizing more precisely (we can accept a sanitized CSV).
3) We'll schedule a perf run (synthetic replay) to validate p95 at target throughput. Suggest week of Dec 7.
4) I'll have Neha (cc) draft a short perf estimate and recommended configuration (GPU type, reserved units).
5) Procurement contact + timelines — loop Claire if we move to reserved capacity.

Attachments: discovery-notes.pdf, ma-plan.xlsx (high-level mutual action plan)

If that looks good I'll book the perf window and share a calendar invite.

— Dylan

Thanks Dylan — appreciate the recap. A few clarifications: 

- 200 ms p95 is effectively a hard target for our payment-fraud scoring pipeline; anything above that increases user friction.
- The 300 rps is our daytime steady state; we do see spikes during peak hours (Black Friday-like) to ~450 rps for ~15-30 minutes.
- We will sanitize and send over the 24-hr traffic sample by EOD Monday.

Claire — looping you for procurement visibility.

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Marcos Silva <marcos@finpay.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery — FinPay latency & throughput needs (technical notes)

Hey team — quick technical write-up based on the numbers Dylan captured. Attaching a short perf-estimate.csv with rough sizing. TL;DR recommendation below.

Key considerations:
- Model: assuming a decoder-only LLM (2-7B equivalent) with avg 120-token in/out.
- Single-turn, batch=1 workload favors low-latency paths; batching hurts p95 in this configuration.
- For 300 rps steady state at p95 <=200 ms, we estimate you need the equivalent of ~8 dedicated inference slots (NVIDIA A10x or comparable) with continuous warm KV cache and autoscale headroom for spikes.

Option A — Hosted API (fastest):
- Pros: quick provisioning, managed autoscaling, and can buy reserved capacity commitments for predictable throughput.
- Cons: multi-tenant runtime; slightly more variance in p95 during sudden unpredicted cluster-wide pressure, but we guarantee baseline throughput for reserved capacity and provide burst capacity policies.
- Expected p95 (reserved capacity config): ~120-180 ms in our benchmarks for similar customers at 300 rps (single-turn).

Option B — Redwood Dedicated (recommended if strict tail-latency isolation required):
- Pros: dedicated GPU pools, predictable tail latencies, isolation from noisy neighbors, SLA-backed uptime/latency targets.
- Cons: longer lead time (provisioning + validation ~7-14 days), higher minimum commitment, procurement paperwork.
- Expected p95: ~90-140 ms for the same workload envelope.

Operational notes:
- We'll run a synthetic perf replay at the requested traffic shape (we need the sample CSV).
- For both options we recommend enabling KV/prefix caching and setting autoscale floor at the estimated slot count.

Next steps I can help with:
- Finalize perf config and run the replay (week of Dec 7).
- Provide an estimated cost delta between Hosted reserved capacity vs Dedicated (monthly commit).

— Neha
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: perf-estimate.csv (sizing assumptions)
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Marcos Silva <marcos@finpay.com>, Claire Johnson <claire.johnson@finpay.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Discovery — FinPay latency & throughput needs (decision follow-up)

Thanks both — great context. Based on Neha's sizing and your hard p95 requirement, here are two pragmatic paths to get you to production quickly while protecting tail latency: 

Option 1 (fastest to production): Hosted API with reserved capacity + burst policy
- We set a reserved baseline sized to Neha's estimate (~8 slots) to cover steady 300 rps.
- Activate burst capacity to cover short spikes to 450 rps (policy-based).
- Expected p95: ~120-180 ms; we'll validate with a perf run.
- Procurement: minimal paperwork — Claire we'd provide a PO-friendly invoice and a short addendum for reserved units.

Option 2 (maximum predictability): Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool)
- We provision a dedicated GPU pool sized per Neha's estimate; isolation reduces tail variance.
- Provisioning + validation ~7-14 days; procurement will need a monthly commit.
- Expected p95: ~90-140 ms.

My suggested path: start with Option 1 to get live quickly, run the perf replay week of Dec 7, and if the perf run shows tail issues we roll to Dedicated (we can plan a canary shift). That gives you fastest time-to-value while keeping a predictable escalation path.

If everyone is aligned I'll: 
- Book the perf window for Dec 8-10 (30 minute replay, Neha to run),
- Generate a short cost comparison for Hosted reserved vs Dedicated by EOD Monday,
- Share procurement steps and a sample PO template for Claire.

Please reply with a quick ACK or propose alternative dates.

— Dylan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
